user.title: Wildfire Monitor
user.description: Get a free MAP_KEY at {map_key_url} — it is stored in the config entry and never shown in the UI.

data.min_frp: Minimum fire radiative power (0 = no filter)

error.cannot_connect: Could not reach the FIRMS servers — check your connection and try again.
error.no_region: FIRMS has no service covering that location. Its feeds are regional and leave parts of the world out; this spot falls in one of the gaps.
error.radius_too_large: The radius is too large — keep it at 310 miles or less. Beyond that FIRMS caps the response and fires would be missing without you noticing.

abort.already_configured: This location is already being monitored.

data.min_frp: Minimum fire radiative power (0 = no filter)

data_description.radius: Used by both NASA FIRMS and NOAA NGFS. The integration keeps metric internally but this setting is shown in miles.
data_description.wind_fires: How many of the nearest fires get the wind at their own coordinates each cycle. Each fire is one MET Norway request per refresh; fires beyond this count carry no wind attributes.
data_description.auto_ignore: Learns which spots radiate month after month — factories, flare stacks, kilns — and hides their routine detections. A spot has to appear across 60 days before it counts, so this does nothing for the first two months. A detection much brighter than that spot's usual output is always shown, so a real fire next to a factory still comes through.
data_description.alert_radius: Separate from the monitoring radius. Fires can be collected for regional smoke awareness without entering the nearby-fire alert zone. Shown in miles.

zones.title: Ignore zones
zones.description:
FIRMS reports heat, not wildfires, so a factory or flare stack shows up every day. Detections inside a zone are dropped before anything else happens to them.

{zones}

add_zone.title: Add an ignore zone
add_zone.description: Drag the pin onto the heat source and size the circle to cover it. Keep it tight: anything inside is invisible to the integration, including a real fire. Maximum {max_miles} miles.

monitoring.title: Seasonal monitoring
monitoring.description: Automatic mode uses full-rate monitoring during fire season and reduced-rate monitoring outside it. Set the polling intervals for both FIRMS and NOAA NGFS below.

data_description.monitoring_mode: Automatic seasonal switches between full and reduced using the dates below. Full monitoring always uses summer cadence. Reduced monitoring always uses off-season cadence. Disabled makes no scheduled wildfire-data requests.

error.zone_radius_too_large: That zone is too large. An ignore zone covers a known heat source, not a region — keep it to 12 miles or less.
error.invalid_season_date: The fire-season start or end date is not a valid month/day.
error.alert_radius_exceeds_monitoring: The nearby-fire alert radius must be the same as or smaller than the monitoring radius.

get_wind.name: Get wind at a fire
get_wind.description: Returns the wind at one fire's own coordinates, right now: where it blows from, how fast, and the smoke offset — the angle between where the wind pushes the smoke and the line from that fire to your monitored location (0 = straight at you, 180 = straight away). Works for any fire, including those beyond the per-cycle wind budget. This is the current wind vector, not a forecast of where the smoke ends up, and never a safety assessment.

entity_id.name: Fire
entity_id.description: The fire entity to look up.

not_a_fire.message: {entity_id} is not an active NASA FIRMS fire entity. The fire may have dropped out of the data since you picked it.

wind_unavailable.message: No wind reading is available for this fire right now. The weather service did not answer, is being rate limited, or its forecast holds no usable step.

truncated.title: Fires are missing from {name}
truncated.description:
FIRMS cut the response off at its cap of {cap} detections per satellite, so every number for this location is too low — the number of fires, the distance to the nearest one, and the strongest fire radiative power. Nothing about those numbers looks wrong, which is why this is here.

Make the request smaller until the cap is no longer reached: shrink the radius, switch the detection window from 7 days back to 24 hours, or raise the minimum confidence or minimum fire radiative power. This notice disappears by itself once a complete response comes back.

orbit_http.title: Satellite observation times are unavailable for {name}
orbit_http.description:
CelesTrak answered HTTP {status} while the integration was fetching orbital elements. Their usage policy asks clients to stop on an error rather than retry it, so this one was not repeated on the update cycle. FIRMS fire data keeps updating as normal — only the previous and next satellite observation are missing.

The integration tries once more after 24 hours and clears this notice by itself if that succeeds; restarting Home Assistant tries again straight away. Worth checking in the meantime: whether this instance can reach celestrak.org, and whether CelesTrak itself is having trouble.
